prose.text: The standard gate set runs in the test-plan §3 order: capability-drift before the default-features workspace nextest, then the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen, then the base-identity bindings close, since no procedure is added. The chunk's own gates come first, all under `--workspace` (test-plan §11 run-scope rule): - the targeted witness/pin run with its collection proof; - the `corpus` package suite; - the three cross-process MCP legs that open the production entry, as a regression check under `--features mcp-server`; - the scope guard.

Absences, each with its reason: - No `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched, so the webview gates are absent. - No boot-path file is touched (`main.rs`, `observability.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `tauri.conf.json`, `capabilities/*.json`; the scope-guard entry proves it), so the boot smoke does not bind (test-plan §3 Boot-smoke gate). - There is no harness live leg and no self-verify. The witness's real processes are re-executed test binaries inside the unit entry. - No dependency is added (`std` file locking plus `blake3`, already a `corpus` dep), so `cargo deny` / `cargo audit` are not listed locally. The CI `supply-chain` job runs them, and the operator CI read asserts it green. - CI runners have no credential store, so the witness clean-skips there. Its non-skip proof is the dev-host entry's `lacks [skip]` atom (test-plan §1 `mcp-incident-read-back-cross-process-coverage` precedent).

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot evaluate on the Linux dev host, because it drives every stage through `wsl.exe` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs:23`). Under the founder deviation of 2026-10-04, its six stages run NATIVELY by hand before the push, as in the two predecessor chunks. They are the six `operator` entries after hygiene, in `Stage::ALL` order, each in the stage isolation of `Linux::cmd`.

Two founder-ruled 2026-10-04 differences from the predecessor's literal form: - Stage 3 runs with `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` pointed at a fresh, per-invocation path under `target/pre-push/`. The ruling is to isolate the cache, never delete `~/.cache/puppeteer`. - Stage 6 seeds a per-invocation data dir with no `rm`.

Because stage 5 (a default-features workspace test run) re-emits the bindings in the no-mcp shape, the `--features mcp-server` regen and the base-identity close are RE-FIRED as `operator` entries after stage 6 and before the push. This is the stage-ORDER lesson the handoff carries.

ONE-SHOT controls at /implement, never listed (they mutate source and revert; the light gate re-runs entries verbatim): - the witness's RED-at-base read against HEAD's unlocked get-then-set; - the mutation check that restores it after the fix (Step 5).

Both readings go in `evidence/mutation-checks.md`, which the second criterion names. That file has no listed producer by construction: /implement writes it from those two runs. The listed, non-mutating `race_free` targeted entry guards the property on every re-run.

The CI read waits 2400 s, against the last measured green run's wall-clock of 1718 s (`a69030a`); its timeout is 2400 + 180. Targeted feature-gated entries carry 5400 s for a cold `--features mcp-server` workspace build.
